samples.question: The grey stroke in this picture is one single closed loop: it never branches, never crosses or touches itself, and it comes back to where it started. Four dots sit on this loop - one green, one red, one blue and one orange. Starting at the green dot and walking along the loop, there are exactly two ways to reach the red dot: one way round and the other way round. Exactly one of the two coloured dots, blue or orange, lies on each of those two ways. Length is measured only as distance travelled along the loop itself, following every bend; straight-line distance across the picture does not count. Take the shorter of the two ways from the green dot to the red dot. Which coloured dot do you pass on it? Answer blue or orange.
